Article.ArticleTitle: Texture analysis of 18F-FDG PET/CT for grading thymic epithelial tumours: usefulness of combining SUV and texture parameters.

Abstract.AbstractText: To retrospectively investigate the SUV-related and heterogeneous texture parameters individually and in combination for differentiating between low-risk and high-risk 18F-FDG-avid thymic epithelial tumours (TETs) with PET/CT.

SUV-related and 6 texture parameters (entropy, homogeneity, dissimilarity, intensity variability [IV], size-zone variability [SZV] and zone percentage [ZP]) were compared between 11 low-risk and 23 high-risk TETs (metabolic tumour volume >10.0 cm3 and SUV≥2.5). Diagnostic performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. The diagnostic value of combining SUV and texture parameters was examined by a scoring system.

High-risk TETs were significantly higher in SUVmax (p=0.022), entropy (p=0.038), IV (p=0.041) and SZV (p=0.045) than low-risk TETs. Diagnostic accuracies of these 4 parameters, dissimilarity and ZP which also showed significance in ROC analysis ranged between 64.7% and 73.5% without significant differences in AUC (range; 0.71 to 0.75) (p≥0.05 each). Each parameter was scored as 0 (negative for high-risk) or 1 (positive for high-risk) according to each threshold criterion, then scores were summed (0 or 1 for low-risk TETs [median; 1]; ï'≥2 for high-risk TETs [median; 4]). The sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of detecting high-risk TETs were 100%, 81.8%, and 94.1%, respectively, with an AUC of 0.99.

The diagnostic performances of individual SUVmax and texture parameters were relatively low. However, combining these parameters can significantly increase diagnostic performance when differentiating between relatively large low- and high-risk 18F-FDG-avid TETs. Advances in knowledge: Combined use of SUVmax and texture parameters can significantly increase the diagnostic performance when differentiating between low-risk and high-risk TETs.
